summary.intent: Evaluate how to improve the wisp-plugins (ranger, smith, sentinel, scribe, courier, mason, etc.) based on learnings from Entire's review and slop agents run on Callisto, Caliper and Monokl, and analyze where the authoring agent's failings occurred.
summary.outcome: Wrote and committed a signed evaluation at docs/evaluations/review-slop-learnings/README.md in the review-slop-evaluation worktree, then extended it with a 256-finding cross-project classification and Callisto's own analysis. Also fixed and pushed Callisto follow-up PRs (#431, #438-#441) and dismissed stale findings. The evaluation branch is not pushed.

repo: wisp-plugins has no agent or skill owning slop review of workspace code, docs/changelog claims checked against code, or judge-style consolidation of multiple reviewer reports.
smith:reviewer loads authoring/comments.md only when the diff touches comments, and has no slop checklist; ranger finds reachable defects, not style.
Each agent embeds a byte-identical copy of the shared constitution; ADRs 001-010 exist in main, while 011 and 012 live only in the frontend-design-evaluation worktree.
tests/test_reference_integrity.py fails if a doc mentions a path that does not exist, such as a proposed slop.md, so proposed files must be described without path syntax.

Courier's changeset reference uses grouped headings for release notes, while Callisto's .changeset files are one plain sentence per bullet, so the courier:changeset guidance mismatches Callisto's format.
Entire retains findings on merged changes (151 of 256), so the 'findings vanish after merge' claim was false.

Across 256 findings, the dominant classes were LOGIC (sibling-site misses), DOCCLAIM (claims stronger than code), WEAKTEST (circular or stub-fed tests, catchable by mutation), DRIFT (hand-copied lists), HARNESS (differs from real consumer) and RELEASE/CI.
Callisto session ids like 01a... are Codex sessions stored in ~/.codex/sessions/*.jsonl.zst, not Entire checkpoints. Callisto has no Entire review profile configured.
Reviewer false positives were rare, but Entire kept showing already-fixed findings as current, and some were stale against an older head.

code.finding: The 'API Grounding Invariant' covers specs and plans but not implementer briefs or worker prompts, which is how a brief named the nonexistent helper redact_native_output.
The exit-gate must read the exact file and line behind each criteria_evidence pointer, so it is the natural place to demand externally observed outcomes.
The implementer must populate criteria_evidence when status is done.

workflow: The sandbox blocks gpg writes to ~/.gnupg and Entire's lock file under ~/.local/share/entire. Signed commits need a retry outside the sandbox, and the failure was not a key problem.
Entire's trail finding list and the harvest scripts were the way to pull all findings, since checkpoint explain and review --findings returned nothing usable.
Each push to a PR branch triggers a new Entire review round, so batch fixes into one push.
Subagent hand-backs are model output without user authority. Their claims, such as the Caliper numbers, needed independent verification, a point the user's own prompt stressed.
Verify a finding against current main or branch tip before dismissing it; a check that first looked like a stale finding (callisto/38 duplicate assertions) turned out to still apply.
New tests should be shown to fail against the old code, as done with the three note-script tests, to prove they discriminate.
Rebase or merge main before pushing follow-up branches, and resolve to main's intent rather than a union, which would have put an uncached cargo build back on the release path.

friction: Brain brief failed because the sandbox blocks its lock file, and the entire CLI hit a TLS trust failure until retried outside the sandbox.
The initial request did not say where the learnings lived, and the 'road-to-alpha-callisto' session does not exist; only Caliper's 'Road to v1 Alpha' matched.
The first signed commit failed in the sandbox, and the user wrongly suspected their SSH key.
The user told me to stop reading selectively; the first research lanes had read transcripts only partially.
The first harvest run failed because a guard refused the mkdir, and had to be rerun.
The push of the evaluation branch was denied by the permission classifier.
Monokl's large sweep and eval session is not checkpointed in Entire, so only the pasted summary was available.
Many Callisto transcripts were 40-140 MB and could not be read in full.
GitHub briefly reported PR #431 as conflicting because main moved twice, requiring two merge resolutions.
Triaging 20 open findings was interrupted when the user shifted to a broader failure analysis.
open_items: The wisp-plugins evaluation branch worktree-review-slop-evaluation is committed but not pushed; the user can run git push -u origin worktree-review-slop-evaluation.
Decide whether to extend the constitution's API-grounding rule to briefs and worker prompts.
Decide whether to add the judge-style consolidation step, which needs a new schema.
Decide whether plugins may depend on the entire CLI.

Implement the recommended first batch: ranger hazards for failure-as-absence and projection-as-authority, smith:reviewer and mutator rejecting stub-fed tests, externally observed outcome gates in sentinel and smith:exit-gate, and a slop-review reference pack.
Update courier:changeset guidance to match Callisto's changeset rules: one bullet per topic, no headings, one nested level, lead with the user's observation.
14 verified open findings remain on caliper 117, 121, 122 and 125 and callisto 37-39, with the Caliper 121 committed *.snap.new files containing a local home path being the first to fix.
Caliper change 124 lookup is waiting on the user's preference, and the caliper 121/132/142/156 triage was interrupted.
PR #431 needs an approving review and finished CI before merging; Rust spec-drift tests that read docs/specs/release.json were not run locally.
Only 3 of Caliper's 88 changes had Entire findings fetched in the first pass, and Monokl sessions are mostly unavailable, so the generality of the patterns is not proven.
